scenario.name: lidar_frozen
scenario.description: The lidar driver gets stuck and keeps sending its last scan with fresh timestamps while the robot drives to its second stop.

ground_truth.summary: Scans keep arriving at the normal rate but never change, so localization and the costmaps work from stale data.

alerts: from about 25.0 s every scan was identical to the one before it, in 1 interval(s) of 5 s; a working lidar never repeats a scan exactly

actions.why: this process was seen dead or silent

diagnosis.root_cause: The lidar stopped delivering new data starting at 25.0 s, as evidenced by identical consecutive scans. This sensor dropout caused the navigation stack to fail to perceive obstacles or update its state, leading to the failure of the pickup P2 mission which was still in progress.
evidence: Mission ended at 26.6 s with pickup P2 still under way.
Lidar status shows identical scans from 25.0 s onwards, indicating a sensor dropout.

decision.note: The diagnosis indicates a sensor dropout where the lidar stopped delivering data. The only action that directly addresses this root cause from the provided list is restarting the lidar driver process. No parameters need restoration, no relocalization is required yet (as the issue is sensor data flow, not pose estimation), and no parcels are blocked by static obstacles (the mission failed due to lack of perception, not a physical blockage requiring deferment/escalation).

incidents.settled: scans at 4.7 Hz and every heartbeat present, 5 s after the fix

alerts: from 47 s (goal: pickup P2) the robot stood still and received no non-zero velocity command for 10 s or more, although a goal was active

actions.target: Remove the 1.1 m obstacle at PICK_A location
actions.why: a message for a person; nothing on the robot changes

diagnosis.root_cause: A 1.1 m obstacle appeared 0.73 m from PICK_A (not in the map) between 22.7 s and 56.7 s, blocking the route or critical area for navigation, causing the controller to fail to make progress and the robot to stand still.
evidence: Obstacle appeared at PICK_A location from 22.7 s to 56.7 s
Controller server ERROR 'Failed to make progress' from 53.9 s
Robot stood still from 47 s with no velocity commands while goal was active

actions.target: Remove the 1.1 m obstacle at PICK_A location

decision.note: The diagnosis is 'blocked_path' caused by a physical obstacle appearing in the map (not in the map). The robot cannot move this obstacle itself. According to the rules: 'Do not defer a parcel or mention an obstacle unless the diagnosis category is blocked_station'. Since the category is 'blocked_path', we do not use 'defer_parcel'. We only escalate for a human to remove the obstacle.

alerts: from 82 s (goal: pickup P2) the robot stood still and received no non-zero velocity command for 10 s or more, although a goal was active

actions.why: nothing was seen blocking PICK_B, where P2 has to go next

actions.target: remove obstacle near PICK_A to clear path to PICK_B
actions.why: a message for a person; nothing on the robot changes

diagnosis.component: path between waypoints PICK_A and PICK_B
diagnosis.root_cause: An obstacle (1.1 m structure) appeared near PICK_A from 22.7 s to 91.7 s, blocking the route to PICK_B. The controller failed to make progress from 88.8 s, causing the robot to stop moving and cancel the P2 pickup attempts.
evidence: Obstacle appeared at PICK_A location (0.73 m away) from 22.7 s to 91.7 s
Robot stood still with no velocity commands from 82 s onwards while goal was active
Controller server ERROR: Failed to make progress from 88.8 s

actions.target: remove obstacle near PICK_A to clear path to PICK_B

decision.note: The diagnosis indicates a physical obstacle blocking the path. Since the robot cannot move obstacles itself, we must defer the parcel (P2) that needs to go to the blocked waypoint next and escalate for human intervention. No parameter restoration, process restart, or costmap clearing is needed as the root cause is an external physical blockage, not a software state error.
